learning_outcomes.text: Explain the classification and physical/chemical properties of fuels (heating value, density, viscosity, moisture, ash, volatile matter, etc.).
Write combustion reactions for stoichiometric and actual combustion conditions; calculate air-fuel ratio, equivalence ratio, and excess air coefficient.
Determine the composition and amount of combustion products using mass and mole balances; interpret flue gas analysis.
Calculate adiabatic flame temperature, heat of combustion, and combustion efficiency based on thermodynamic fundamentals.
Explain combustion-related pollutants (CO, NOx, SOx, particulates, volatile organic compounds, etc.) and their formation mechanisms.
Evaluate different fuels and combustion systems in terms of efficiency, emissions, and environmental impact, and recommend suitable fuel/combustion conditions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to combustion and classification of fuels
Combustion and combustion equations, ignition temperature, dew point temperature and properties of air

AFR, types of combustion (theoretical complete combustion, complete combustion, incomplete combustion and partial incomplete combustion), stoichiometric air, excess air, excess air percentage, incomplete air and incomplete air percentage
General reaction equations in terms of introductory quantities, calculation of volume fractions and maximum CO2, analysis of incomplete combustion and partial incomplete combustion products
Reaction enthalpy and combustion enthalpy Heating values of fuels Problems related to combustion products
Entropy changes of reacting systems Thermal dissociation and its effect on adiabatic flame temperature
Effects of combustion wastes on human health and the environment and methods of elimination
bibliography: Yakıtlar ve Yanma, Mustafa Acaroğlu, Nobel Yayınları
Combustion / Irvin Glassman, Imprint San Diego, Calif.: Academic Press, 3rd ed., 1996.
